title: Validate Password Prefix Against Security Rules
real_world_story: A security system maintains a collection of approved password prefixes used by different authentication policies. When a new password is submitted, the system needs to determine whether its starting characters match any stored security prefix.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Stored security prefixes and a password to analyze
real_world_connection.target_represents: Whether the password begins with any registered security prefix
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: A Trie that stores prefixes character by character for efficient prefix searching

problem_statement: Given N registered security prefixes and a password string, determine whether the password starts with at least one of the registered prefixes. Print the first matching prefix in lexicographic order, or -1 if no registered prefix matches.
task: Use a Trie to search whether the password begins with any registered security prefix.
input_format: The first line contains an integer N. The second line contains N space-separated lowercase security prefixes. The third line contains the password string.
output_format: Print the lexicographically smallest registered prefix that is a prefix of the password. If no registered prefix matches, print -1.
constraints: Prefixes and password contain only lowercase English letters

examples.explanation: The password begins with the registered prefix 'safe'.
The password does not begin with any of the registered security prefixes.

expected_algorithm.name: Trie Operations
expected_algorithm.reason: A Trie stores prefixes character by character and allows efficient prefix-based searching.

complexity.where: T is the total length of stored prefixes and P is the length of the password.

hint: Insert every registered prefix into a Trie.
Traverse the Trie using the characters of the password.
Track registered prefixes encountered during the traversal.
Return the lexicographically smallest matching prefix.
real_world_takeaway: Trie structures are useful for efficiently managing prefix-based security rules, authentication patterns, and policy lookups.
